working_definition: LPLC1 is an adult Drosophila lobula plate-lobula columnar visual projection neuron whose wide-field dendrites innervate all layers of the lobula plate and lobula layers 2-5B, with the cell body in the dorsal lateral cell body rind. It projects cholinergically to a posterior optic glomerulus in the PVLP and functions as a loom-detecting neuron with approximately 62 cells per optic lobe.
searches_performed: lobula plate lobula columnar neuron (core anatomical type, ontology: fbbt)

best_match.fbbt_definition: Lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron whose cell body lies in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind (Wu et al., 2016). Its processes extend the full depth of the lobula plate, being sparser in layer 1 (Wu et al., 2016). In the lobula, its main dendritic arbors are in layers 2-5B (Wu et al., 2016; Tanaka and Clark, 2022). Presynaptic sites are observed in the boundary of lobula layers 3/4 (Wu et al., 2016). Its arbors span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC1 cells (Wu et al., 2016). It projects to a posterior optic glomerulus of the PVLP, at the boundary with the PLP (Wu et al., 2016). There are around 62 cells of this type (Wu et al., 2016). They are cholinergic (Davis et al., 2020).

justification: FBbt:00111762 is named 'lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC1', which is the canonical anatomical name for this cluster. The FBbt definition agrees with every defining feature of the cluster: lobula plate innervation across all layers (sparser in layer 1), lobula dendrites in layers 2-5B, dorsal lateral cell body rind position, approximately 25-column wide-field arbors, projection to the posterior PVLP optic glomerulus at the PLP boundary, approximately 62 cells, and cholinergic neurotransmitter. There is no residual ambiguity. The cluster label 'LPLC1' is simply the abbreviated form of the FBbt label. Both flags are false because this is a confident exact match with no unconfirmed equivalence.

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: Lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron whose cell body lies in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind (Wu et al., 2016). It has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer (Klapoetke et al., 2017). In the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4 (Wu et al., 2016; Tanaka and Clark, 2022). Its arbors span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells (Wu et al., 2016). It projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4 (Wu et al., 2016). There are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe (Wu et al., 2016) and they are cholinergic (Davis et al., 2020).
other_candidates.reason_rejected: LPLC2 is a distinct sister type: different lobula layer innervation pattern (layers 4 and 5B versus 2-5B), different cell count (~80 versus ~62), and projects to an anterior glomerulus rather than the posterior one. Returned in search results as a related LPLC-class neuron but clearly a different cell type.

recommendation: Accept FBbt:00111762 as the exact match for cluster LPLC1. No further curation action required for this mapping.
